documents.unit: Academic Affairs Division / Office of the Provost
documents.title: UL Lafayette Guidance on Generative Artificial Intelligence in the Classroom
tiers: Sample statement encouraging use of AI-generated material
documents.summary: University guidance that sets no rule itself but asks colleges, departments and faculty to write AI policies, lists areas a policy should cover (permitted uses, responsible use, citation, penalties) and gives three sample syllabus statements (prohibit, mixed, encourage). Students must learn each class's rules.
documents.stance_why: The guidance states that 'All faculty have academic freedom in their classrooms and will be the ones to determine what constitutes proper use of GAI', and offers sample statements ranging from prohibition to encouragement, so the university sets no stance and hands the decision to instructors.

units.why: Opening framing says GAI 'is rapidly changing higher education'; it is context for the guidance, coded as institutional framework.
units.anchor: The proliferation of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) tools is rapidly changing higher education.

units.why: States that AI 'can also deliver results that contain significant inaccuracies and conscious and unconscious biases', a warning that outputs are flawed; P31 chosen because the point is unreliable output.
units.anchor: AI can also deliver results that contain significant inaccuracies and conscious and unconscious biases.
units.fit_note: Also names bias as a concern (P53) but framed as output reliability.

units.why: Says the university is 'training the future workforce' that is 'increasingly exposed to and engaging with Generative AI tools', a career-readiness reason for engaging with AI.
units.anchor: a workforce that is increasingly exposed to and engaging with Generative AI tools
units.fit_note: Does not say courses teach AI; only that the workforce encounters it.

units.why: Says 'GAI is an undeniable presence' so the university must continue pedagogy; acknowledges AI cannot be avoided.
units.anchor: we now do so in an academic ecosystem where GAI is an undeniable presence
units.fit_note: Says presence is undeniable rather than that use cannot be verified or prevented.

units.why: 'It is our responsibility to ensure that we engage with AI in a manner that safeguards academic integrity' states the principle guiding the guidance, an institution-level framework.
units.anchor: engage with AI in a manner that safeguards academic integrity

units.why: Scope sentence: 'applies to student intellectual coursework products at the graduate and undergraduate levels', defining what the guidance covers.
units.anchor: This guidance applies to student intellectual coursework products at the graduate and undergraduate levels.
units.fit_note: Defines scope but not AI itself.

units.why: Purpose statement 'to promote ethical engagement with AI across the University' is a stated principle, so framework.
units.anchor: The purpose of this guidance is to promote ethical engagement with AI across the University.

units.why: The guidance 'encourages academic colleges, departments, and individual faculty to develop specific policies', so units below the university may set their own rules; P85 chosen over instructor-level P04 because colleges and departments come first.
units.anchor: encourages academic colleges, departments, and individual faculty to develop specific policies for their students

units.why: 'will vary significantly across disciplines, and even among classes' and ranges from restrictions to 'complete integration', so the rule is set per course (P04).
units.anchor: restrictions, guardrails, or complete integration of GAI into assignments, will vary significantly

units.why: Says rules depend on 'the skills and learning outcomes they seek to impart', tying AI decisions to learning objectives.
units.anchor: depending on the skills and learning outcomes they seek to impart

units.why: 'All faculty have academic freedom ... and will be the ones to determine what constitutes proper use', the decision is delegated to instructors.
units.anchor: will be the ones to determine what constitutes proper use of GAI in their classroom

units.why: 'it is the students' responsibility to familiarize themselves with relevant expectations and policies' puts the burden of learning each class's rules on students.
units.anchor: it is the students’ responsibility to familiarize themselves with relevant expectations and policies

units.why: 'Because different classes may have different AI policies' means a course's rules are not uniform across courses; states non-carryover.
units.anchor: Because different classes may have different AI policies
units.policy: Different classes may have different AI policies.
units.fit_note: Says policies differ across classes, not explicitly that permissions do not carry over.

units.why: Tells faculty to 'Define the range of uses of AI and be explicit about what you allow in your class', a call to state expectations explicitly.
units.anchor: be explicit about what you allow in your class.

units.why: Example use 'brainstorm and conduct preliminary research' is a permitted use listed for policies to consider; brainstorming is the best match.
units.anchor: Use of GAI to brainstorm and conduct preliminary research for assignments.

units.why: Example use 'summarize articles and other readings' is a study aid use that instructors may allow.
units.anchor: Use of GAI to summarize articles and other readings.

units.why: Example use 'analyze quantitative or qualitative data' instructors may allow.
units.anchor: Use of GAI to analyze quantitative or qualitative data.

units.why: Example use 'proof-reading, grammar assistance, or to adjust style and tone' is editing support.
units.anchor: Use of GAI for proof-reading, grammar assistance, or to adjust style and tone.

units.why: Example use 'develop graphics or foreign language translations' is a permitted use not matching any listed type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Use of GAI to develop graphics or foreign language translations.
units.uncovered_note: AI may be used to make graphics or translations for coursework.

units.why: Example use 'produce a draft or outline ... critically edited and expanded upon by the student' permits a draft under the condition of student editing; fits writing support with a condition.
units.anchor: critically edited and expanded upon by the student.
units.fit_note: Allows AI-produced draft if student critically edits and expands it, beyond editing one's own writing.

units.why: 'Reaffirm that students are responsible for accuracy, bias, and integrity of any use of GAI' makes students accountable for what AI produces.
units.anchor: students are responsible for accuracy, bias, and integrity of any use of GAI

units.why: Instructors should 'Articulate ... the limitations of AI and their responsibility to fact-check AI', i.e. students must verify output.
units.anchor: their responsibility to fact-check AI for both accuracy and bias in results

units.why: 'Define the importance of being transparent about AI usage' sets transparency as a principle to communicate.
units.anchor: Define the importance of being transparent about AI usage.
units.fit_note: Asks instructors to explain transparency rather than requiring a statement.

units.why: 'require citations where there is AI usage' in courses where AI is allowed, a disclosure requirement.
units.anchor: require citations where there is AI usage

units.why: Documentation alternatives: 'saving and uploading for instructor review transcripts of GAI interaction, or screenshots', i.e. keep and submit transcripts.
units.anchor: saving and uploading for instructor review transcripts of GAI interaction, or screenshots of GAI sessions

units.why: 'encourage students to participate in trainings that teach proper AI usage' recommends AI training for students.
units.anchor: encourage students to participate in trainings that teach proper AI usage

units.why: Instructors should 'Be specific about how these apply to different types of AI', distinguishing grammar assistance from other GAI; a penalty-specification rule, closest to stating penalties in advance.
units.anchor: potentially differentiating between grammar/punctuation assistance GAI and other forms of GAI
units.fit_note: Asks that rules differentiate types of AI, which also touches routine-feature exemption (P100).

units.why: Says unauthorized GAI use 'constitutes academic misconduct', classifying misuse under integrity.
units.anchor: then the use of GAI in that course constitutes academic misconduct

units.why: Covers use 'to author or assist with any portion of the final assignments or intellectual scaffolding', so where AI is banned the ban covers assistance and drafts, not just final text.
units.anchor: author or assist with any portion of the final assignments or intellectual scaffolding
units.frag_start: to author or assist with any portion
units.fit_note: Extends the prohibition to assistance and preliminary scaffolding.

units.why: 'Indicate grade penalties (if applicable) clearly and specifically' tells instructors to state penalties in advance.
units.anchor: Indicate grade penalties (if applicable) clearly and specifically.

units.why: Sample prohibition: 'Use of artificial intelligence (AI) to generate material is strictly prohibited', a template for a no-AI course.
units.anchor: Use of artificial intelligence (AI) to generate material is strictly prohibited.

units.why: Same sample states AI-generated submissions 'will be considered a violation of the University's academic integrity policy'.
units.anchor: will be considered a violation of the University’s academic integrity policy
units.frag_start: Submission of material generated by AI

units.why: Sample says it applies 'This includes AI-generated material that you have summarized or edited', closing the loophole of edited output.
units.anchor: This includes AI-generated material that you have summarized or edited.

units.why: Bracketed exclusion 'AI-supported tools providing spelling and grammar checks' exempts routine tools from the sample ban.
units.anchor: This excludes AI-supported tools providing spelling and grammar checks.

units.why: Sample mixed policy permits GAI 'for brainstorming and research'; closest to brainstorming permission.
units.anchor: you may use generative AI tools for brainstorming and research
units.frag_start: In this class, you may use

units.why: Same sample requires students to 'develop and compose your final assignments independently', do not let AI produce submitted work.
units.anchor: must develop and compose your final assignments independently

units.why: Sample invites students to 'email me' with questions about exceptions, so ask the instructor when unsure.
units.anchor: If you have questions or suggestions for potential exceptions, please email me

units.why: Sample encouraging policy: 'Use of artificial intelligence (AI) to generate a first draft of an assignment is permitted', with review required.
units.anchor: generate a first draft of an assignment is permitted
units.frag_start: Use of artificial intelligence (AI) to generate a first
units.frag_end: review and revise any AI-generated material before submission.
units.fit_note: Covers drafts of assignments generally, not code specifically.

units.why: Sample requires students to 'review and revise any AI-generated material before submission' so they stay responsible for what they submit.
units.anchor: you must review and revise any AI-generated material before submission
units.frag_start: but you must review and revise
units.fit_note: Review and revise requirement rather than a fact-check requirement.

units.why: Sample states 'You are responsible for the content of any work submitted for this course.'
units.anchor: You are responsible for the content of any work submitted for this course.

units.why: Sample requires 'transparent about your use of AI-generated material by following citation and documentation guidelines'.
units.anchor: you are required to be transparent about your use of AI-generated material
units.frag_end: documentation guidelines provided in this course.

units.why: Sample warns AI 'prone to factual errors, incorrect or fabricated citations, and misinterpretations', a verify-output warning.
units.anchor: they are prone to factual errors, incorrect or fabricated citations, and misinterpretations of abstract concepts

units.why: Provides 'Resources for instructors' including citation guides (APA, MLA, Chicago) and 'Sample Assignments redesigned to incorporate GAI', support for instructors in designing around AI.
units.anchor: Sample Assignments redesigned to incorporate GAI
units.frag_start: How to Cite ChatGPT from the APA
units.fit_note: Resources are sample assignments and citation guides, not workshops.

documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Guidelines
documents.summary: Short Graduate School page framing GAI use in scholarly work around transparency, ethics, intellectual property and integrity. The saved page text gives principles and links; the linked guidelines document was not in the saved text.
documents.stance_why: The page states principles only ('emphasizes transparency, faculty involvement, and ethical use in scholarly work') and sets no permission or ban in the saved text, so no stance is taken and details are left to the linked guidelines and faculty.

units.why: Graduate School says it is 'committed to preparing the next generation of researchers with integrity and ethical awareness', a principle framing.
units.anchor: committed to preparing the next generation of researchers with integrity and ethical awareness
units.frag_start: The University of Louisiana at Lafayette is

units.why: Says it is 'essential to use these tools responsibly' as GAI integrates into research, teaching and communication.
units.anchor: it is essential to use these tools responsibly

units.why: Guidance 'emphasizes transparency, faculty involvement, and ethical use in scholarly work', stating the guideline principles for scholarly use.
units.anchor: emphasizes transparency, faculty involvement, and ethical use in scholarly work
units.fit_note: Names principles of scholarly use but no specific rule.

units.why: Addresses 'authorial consent, intellectual property, and academic integrity', concerns the guidelines cover; IP chosen as the most concrete.
units.anchor: It addresses key concerns such as authorial consent, intellectual property, and academic integrity
units.fit_note: Also authorial consent and integrity, not only copyright.

units.why: 'ensuring that GAI supports research rather than replacing the critical insight and creativity of human scholars' says AI should not replace human thinking.
units.anchor: GAI supports research rather than replacing the critical insight and creativity of human scholars

units.why: Closing line: GAI 'cannot replicate human creativity, insight, or judgment' and must be 'paired with expertise and integrity'.
units.anchor: it cannot replicate human creativity, insight, or judgment
units.frag_start: GAI can enhance research, teaching, and
units.fit_note: States limits of AI rather than a rule that students stay primary thinker.

units.why: Points to the Academic Affairs, Distance Learning and Communications guidance for other areas of campus, reflecting different areas guided by different units.
units.anchor: For further guidance across other areas of campus, see
units.frag_end: Office of Communications & Marketing: AI Guidelines
units.fit_note: Refers readers to unit-specific guidance rather than authorizing units to set rules.

notes: Graduate School page text is mostly framing; the linked Graduate School GAI Guidelines document was not in the saved text, so only the visible principles were coded.
